paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Psalm 91 is about WHERE you live, not just what you get. The psalm opens with someone who "dwells in the shelter of the Most High" (Psalm 91:1), and later says "Because you have made the LORD your dwelling" (Psalm 91:9). Every promise about the arrow, the plague and the dark hangs on that one choice to make God your home. I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, a place to stay and a place to be safe are two different things!

Now look at what the psalm says that shelter holds. It covers every hour: the night, the day, the darkness and noon (Psalm 91:5-6). It gives you a God who covers you with His feathers, sends angels to guard you and says "I will be with him in trouble" (Psalm 91:4, 11, 15). Notice that last promise. The psalm never says trouble won't come near the world. It says the LORD will be with you in it, and I think that's the part a tired baker needs to hear most.

And the psalm ends with the LORD Himself speaking. He says He will deliver the one who loves Him and knows His name, and He closes with "With long life I will satisfy him and show him My salvation" (Psalm 91:14, 16). So the best gift isn't escaping the lion. It's seeing God's salvation. Love Him, know Him, call on Him, and make Him your home, baker. That's a bakery that never closes.
